anya (devex): Heads-up: hit a really confusing onboarding hiccup with the sampleapp/docker quickstart. Thought it was a bug in our example prompts but it was auth.

tom (sdk): what happened?

anya (devex): ran local quickstart, set PROJECT_TOKEN for the demo workspace and forgot ORG_TOKEN was in my shell. sampleapp started sending requests under the org account.

neha (platform): hmm, we intentionally made project-scoped tokens higher priority in the docs. CLI should prefer PROJECT_TOKEN.

anya (devex): yeah docs say PROJECT_TOKEN first. but the helper in the container image calls into the shared keyring and the keyring lookup returns the org token which wins.

kevin (eng-runtime): can you paste the exact env + repro?

anya (devex): `export ORG_TOKEN=org_xyz; export PROJECT_TOKEN=proj_abc; docker build . && docker run --rm demo` -> analytics show org workspace active.

tom (sdk): ok that tells me two problems: (1) precedence in runtime loader, (2) keyring entries not namespaced by project id so they shadow each other.

neha (platform): agreed. we should namespace keyring keys with a prefix like `redwood:project:<proj_id>:token` so a cached org token doesn't overwrite project-scoped creds.

kevin (eng-runtime): low-risk fix: change loader order to check explicit env vars first, then keyring. something like:
```
// pseudo
const token = process.env.PROJECT_TOKEN || process.env.ORG_TOKEN || keyring.get(currentProject)
```
That avoids accidental cross-project calls even if keyring has an org token.

tom (sdk): I'll open a tiny patch to flip the check and add a unit test matrix for env combos. also adding keyring namespacing PR after that.

anya (devex): can we also log a warning when both envs exist? a simple startup banner makes a world of difference for new users: `Both ORG_TOKEN and PROJECT_TOKEN set; using PROJECT_TOKEN` with a link to the quickstart doc.

neha (platform): yes, and CI sanity scan would help teams detect accidental ORG_TOKEN leaks in Dockerfiles. I've seen org tokens accidentally baked into images before.

kevin (eng-runtime): ops-bot can we add a linter check to the image build pipeline to fail on ORG_TOKEN in Dockerfile or build args?

ops-bot: created issue #412: add Dockerfile/CI scan to detect ORG_TOKEN usage in builds. Assigned to neha.

tom (sdk): PR: https://git.redwood/sdks/commit/flip-precedence-101 — flips env order in loader, adds tests for (only ORG, only PROJECT, both, none). CI green locally.

anya (devex): perfect. I'll update the quickstart example and the sampleapp Dockerfile to `ENV ORG_TOKEN=\"\"` so stray credentials are cleared in the image. Also adding a short note in the UX docs about env precedence.

neha (platform): after the keyring namespacing PR lands, we'll add a migration note for users with existing cached tokens: how to rotate/delete org tokens from the keyring.

kevin (eng-runtime): one more thing: consider a safety net in runtime to reject cross-account requests if token scope doesn't match the current project metadata. Could avoid accidental billing.

tom (sdk): good idea, adding an optional strict-mode env var `REDWOOD_STRICT_AUTH=1` that enforces token/project matching and fails fast.

anya (devex): lovely. this thread saved several hours of debugging for me. will close after docs + PR merge. :raised_hands:
